title: Chapter 1 — Welcome to Appliance IQ
intro: This is not another sales manual. This is a system built from 20 years on the floor — designed to teach you how to think, not just what to say.

sections.title: What This Program Is
sections.content:
Most sales training teaches you scripts. This program teaches you a process.

The difference matters. Scripts break the moment a customer says something unexpected. A process adapts to every customer, every channel, every situation — because it is built on understanding people, not memorizing lines.

This program is called Appliance IQ for a reason. IQ is not about being the smartest person in the room. It is about understanding your customer, your product, your process, and yourself well enough to consistently help people make confident buying decisions.

Everything in this system was built from real experience on real sales floors. Not theory. Not textbooks. Thousands of customer conversations, hundreds of coaching sessions, and every mistake you can imagine — turned into a system that works.

sections.title: The 10 Steps of Selling
sections.content:
The foundation of everything you will learn is the 10 Steps of Selling. Every chapter, every technique, every coaching rule connects back to these steps.

Step 1 — Engagement. Step 2 — Rapport. Step 3 — Discovery. Step 4 — Needs Assessment. Step 5 — Wants Assessment. Step 6 — Product Recommendation. Step 7 — Presentation. Step 8 — Objection Handling. Step 9 — Closing. Step 10 — Follow-up.

These are not suggestions. They are the structure of a professional sale. Skip one and the rest get harder. Follow all ten and closing becomes the easiest part of the conversation.

You will learn each step in detail throughout this program. For now, understand that these 10 steps are your operating system. When things go well, they explain why. When things go wrong, they tell you where to look.

sections.title: How to Use This Program
sections.content:
This program is organized into 16 volumes. You do not need to complete them in order — but the first five volumes build the foundation that everything else depends on.

Volumes I through V cover the core sales process. If you master nothing else, master these. They will make you money.

Volumes VI through XI cover specialized selling — trade accounts, builder channels, attach rates. These matter when you are ready to expand beyond the retail floor.

Volumes XII through XVI cover psychology, metrics, AI tools, operations, and leadership. These turn a good salesperson into a complete professional.

Every chapter ends with a Coaching Rule — a checklist that managers can use to evaluate and develop the skill. If you are using this on your own, use those rules to evaluate yourself honestly.

sections.title: One Principle Before You Start
sections.content:
Before you read another chapter, understand this: the quality of your career in sales will be determined by your habits, not your talent.

The people earning the most on the floor are not the smartest. They are the most consistent. They prepare more. They learn more. They follow up more. They care more.

This program gives you the knowledge. What you do with it is up to you.

Preparation beats luck. Consistency beats talent. Habits beat intentions. That philosophy runs through every chapter you are about to read.
